findings.impact: `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime`, so `math.floor` or `math.ceil` raises `TypeError` when `build_cursor` invokes this method; the endpoint returns a server error instead of audit logs.
findings.root_cause: The new paginator uses numeric-key conversion for a paginator whose only call site orders by a datetime field.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the datetime-to-millisecond key conversion used by `DateTimePaginator`, or derive this paginator from `DateTimePaginator`.
findings.title: Optimized audit-log pagination crashes when generating a cursor for datetime rows
findings.trigger: An authorized user requests `optimized_pagination=true` for an organization containing at least one audit-log entry.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 840 exists verbatim. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime` field (confirmed in auditlogentry.py:69). The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` directly on the datetime value without converting to timestamp first, unlike `DateTimePaginator` which uses `float(value.strftime('%s.%f'))`. This will raise TypeError when the paginator is used with audit logs ordered by `-datetime`.

findings.body: Django querysets reject slices with a negative start, raising `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`; the request returns an unhandled server error rather than a page or validation error.
findings.failure_mode: The newly introduced advanced-pagination branch deterministically raises for the input it is intended to support.
findings.impact: Django querysets reject slices with a negative start, raising `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`; the request returns an unhandled server error rather than a page or validation error.
findings.root_cause: The implementation incorrectly assumes Django ORM querysets support negative slicing.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError`, or implement reverse traversal through ordering and nonnegative slices rather than negative queryset indices.
findings.title: The advertised negative-offset path uses unsupported Django queryset slicing
findings.trigger: An authorized audit-log request enables optimized pagination and supplies a cursor with a negative offset, for example `cursor=0:-1:0`.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 882 exists verbatim: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`. When `enable_advanced_features=True` and `cursor.offset < 0`, `start_offset` is set to the negative offset (line 880). Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The endpoint passes `enable_advanced_features=True` (line 82).

raw_findings.body: Because a slice starting at `offset` can return at most `limit + extra` rows, its length cannot equal `offset + limit + extra` when `offset > 0`; the extra row is not removed and the paginator can return more than the requested page size or duplicate a row across pages.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Boundary cleanup is skipped for positive-offset reverse traversal, corrupting page size and cursor continuity.
raw_findings.impact: Because a slice starting at `offset` can return at most `limit + extra` rows, its length cannot equal `offset + limit + extra` when `offset > 0`; the extra row is not removed and the paginator can return more than the requested page size or duplicate a row across pages.
raw_findings.root_cause: The slice's absolute stop position is incorrectly used as though it were the maximum number of returned rows.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compare the fetched length with `limit + extra` rather than adding the starting offset, and add a regression test for positive-offset previous cursors with a changed boundary row.
